predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the protectorate inside its 'British East Africa' shape (1961-1968), which the british-east-africa dossier closes for Botswana at 30 September 1966. British Bechuanaland south of the Molopo was a different territory, 'incorporated into the Cape Colony in 1895 and now forms part of South Africa'.

capitals.name: Gaborone
capitals.note: Protectorate page infobox 'Capital: Mafikeng (1885-1965); Gaborone (1965-1966)'; Botswana page: 'The seat of government was moved in 1965 from Mahikeng in South Africa, to the newly established Gaborone'. The move precedes the state, so there is no capital_move event. Coordinates from the gazetteer (Natural Earth).

correction.text: the Bechuanaland Protectorate within its frontiers, independent as the Republic of Botswana on 30 September 1966: the same land as the 1967 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins 1967 against 'Bechuanaland became an independent Commonwealth republic under its current name on 30 September 1966.' The land lies inside Cliopatria's British East Africa shape until 1968; that overlap is for the british-east-africa dossier to resolve.

577,330 km2 for 1967-1989 against the infobox 'Total: 581,730 km2' (ratio 0.99). Gazetteer: 2,000 cells against 2,010 for modern Botswana. The row's listed modern countries (Namibia, South Africa) are overlap of cells along the frontier.

577,461 km2 for 1990-2023, 131 km2 (0.02%) above the earlier shape, its southern edge moving from 26.84 S to 26.91 S. The page records no border change in 1990; the December 1999 ICJ ruling on Kasikili Island is nine years later and confirms title. Treated as shape refinement, no ledger event.

ledger.note: 30 September 1966: the Bechuanaland Protectorate becomes the independent Republic of Botswana under Seretse Khama. 'Bechuanaland became an independent Commonwealth republic under its current name on 30 September 1966'; Khama 'was elected as the first president'. The protectorate page: 'It became independent as the Republic of Botswana on 30 September 1966.'

wars.name: Kasikili/Sedudu Island dispute (Botswana and Namibia)
wars.outcome: 'A long-running dispute over the northern border with Namibia's Caprivi Strip was the subject of a ruling by the International Court of Justice in December 1999. It ruled that Kasikili Island belongs to Botswana.'
wars.note: A boundary dispute, not a war; listed so the reviewer sees it was considered. The page dates only the ruling, which is why from and to are both 1999; it calls the dispute 'long-running' and gives no start. It confirmed Botswana's existing title, so there is no gain event, and the island is not a contest zone the grid can draw.

wars.name: Rhodesian Bush War (spillover into Botswana)
wars.outcome: No territory changed hands. ZIPRA guerrillas used bases in Botswana; the Rhodesian forces fought the war on the Zimbabwe side.
wars.note: Bush War page: the guerrillas operated 'using bases in Zambia and Botswana'. Botswana page: 'At the time of independence, Botswana had no armed forces.' Botswana was not a combatant, and no page opened describes a Rhodesian occupation or border change. Span clamped by the reviewer to the state's life (the war began in 1964, before independence on 30 September 1966).

certainty.note: The frontier is the protectorate's: its northern boundary 'was formally extended northward by the British to include Ngamiland' (30 June 1890, protectorate page) and the Caprivi strip was created by the Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty. The northern frontier with Namibia's Caprivi Strip was disputed until the ICJ ruling on Kasikili Island in December 1999.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Republic of Botswana' begins 1967 against independence on 30 September 1966, so a 1966 keyframe is added; it overlaps British East Africa (1961-1968) in 1967-1968. The page does not mention Rhodesian or South African incursions into Botswana, nor a Kazungula border crossing, nor Sedudu by that name; the Zambia border is described only as 'a tiny border of Chobe District'. The protectorate page does not describe a 1961-1965 decision to move to Gaborone, a 1960 constitution or the South Africa Act schedule of 1910; it dates a general election to 1 March 1965 and lists Khama's tenure from 3 March 1965 to independence (the self-government that preceded it). Rulers omitted. Page budget: two pages plus the Rhodesian Bush War page shared with other dossiers. native_names left empty: no page read gives one.
